title: The dialog to create new file from clipboard contents onto Desktop is modal and block Plasma
line: Pasting text onto the desktop no longer freezes the panels while the file name dialog is open.
explanation: Pasting clipboard text onto the desktop goes through KIO::paste, which asks for a file name with PasteDialog (and, if the name is taken, a RenameDialog). Both were run with exec() as application-modal dialogs, so every other plasmashell window, panels included, ignored mouse input until they were closed. The dialogs are now window-modal: they still block the window they belong to (e.g. Dolphin's main window), but plasmashell has no parent window for them, so its panels and launcher keep working.

commits.message:
paste: make the paste dialogs window-modal

The filename and "File Already Exists" dialogs were application-modal, so
pasting onto the desktop blocked all of plasmashell, panels included,
until they were closed. They now only block the window they belong to.

BUG: 522157

media.caption: Ctrl+V on the desktop, then clicking the Kickoff button twice: nothing opens while the name dialog is up
Same steps with the fix: Kickoff opens while the name dialog stays open
Pasting again with the same name: the File Already Exists dialog also blocks the Kickoff button
With the fix the panel stays usable with that dialog open too

review.text: The goal and repo (KIO) are right, and making the dialogs non-application-modal unblocks the Plasma panel, but keeping synchronous `QDialog::exec()` nested event loops on parentless non-blocking dialogs inside `KIO::PasteJob` is unsafe. Because `plasmashell` remains interactive, a second Ctrl+V stacks another `exec()` loop so accepting/cancelling the first dialog stalls until the second is closed, and destroying or killing the `PasteJob` during `exec()` can run `DeferredDelete` while `PasteJobPrivate::slotStart()` is still on the stack (use-after-free). Since `PasteJob` is already an async `KJob` and `paste.cpp`'s helper functions are internal, the prompts should be converted to async `show()`/`open()` + `finished` signals instead of relying on `Qt::WindowModal` + `exec()`.
changes: Replace the synchronous `PasteDialog::exec()`, `RenameDialog::exec()`, and `StatJob::exec()` calls in `src/widgets/paste.cpp` / `PasteJob` with asynchronous `show()` + `QDialog::finished` (and `KJob::result`) handling using `WA_DeleteOnClose` and `parent ? Qt::WindowModal : Qt::NonModal`, guarding job/widget lifetime across callbacks.
Audit `chooseFormatAndUrl()`'s `KMessageBox::information(widget, ...)` path as well so an expired clipboard format doesn't still pop an application-modal dialog in `plasmashell`.
Re-verify stacked/concurrent Ctrl+V pastes on the desktop by accepting the first dialog while the second is still open, and test cancelling/destroying the containment while a paste dialog is open.

reviews.text: Right repo and right cause: PasteDialog (private) and the File Already Exists RenameDialog were application-modal, and the screenshots show Kickoff opening with the dialog up after the change, so the reported blocking is gone. But the dialogs still run in nested exec() loops, and now that the rest of the app stays interactive those loops become re-entrant: a second Ctrl+V (or a text drop, which uses the same dialog) stacks a second nested loop, and because nested loops unwind LIFO, accepting the first dialog does nothing until the second one is closed. The rig only tested the order that happens to work. KIO maintainers avoid widening nested-loop re-entrancy in a framework used by every app, so this is unlikely to be accepted as-is.
changes: Make the filename/rename step asynchronous in PasteJobPrivate (dialog->open() with the job continuing on finished, no exec()), keeping the window-modal modality, so no nested loop is left to re-enter
If that's judged too large: at minimum block re-entrant pastes (e.g. FolderModel ignores paste/drop while its PasteJob is still asking for a name) and test accepting the first of two dialogs
Re-verify the panels stay usable, OK/Cancel/Rename/Overwrite still work, and Dolphin's own window is still blocked while the dialog is open
